newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says recent German prices mostly moderate.
newsitem.headline: Buba says recent German prices mostly moderate.

text.p: German prices have been mostly moderate even as external factors helped fan some inflationary pressures, the Bundesbank said in its March report.
"The price climate in Germany has until recently been largely relaxed even though some inflationary pressures were triggered by external factors," the central bank wrote.
Even as oil prices declined in February, prices in dollars for commodities, food and other goods have climbed again, the Bundesbank explained.
These comments came after several Bundesbank officials had in recent weeks said the sharp appreciation of the U.S. dollar was not affecting German inflation rates, still running below two percent.

On the other hand the Bundesbank also said that consumer prices, which had been risen quite sharply in January in the wake of higher administrative prices and the severe winter weather, did not continue their sharp rise in February.
In February the West German inflation rate eased back to 1.8 percent from 1.9 percent in January, the Bundesbank said.
